sources.entry: RustFS | High-performance S3-compatible object storage written in Rust

summary.one_liner: RustFS is a high-performance, distributed, S3-compatible object storage system written in Rust, released under Apache 2.0.
summary.what_it_does: RustFS is a distributed object storage server built in Rust that aims for broad S3 API compatibility for supported features. The README lists support for erasure-coded distributed and single-node modes, bitrot protection, healing and a scanner, versioning, Object Lock, server-side encryption, IAM/policies, OIDC/SSO, bucket replication, site replication, lifecycle management, event notifications, and a web console. It also documents OpenStack Swift API and Keystone authentication (behind an opt-in cargo feature), FTPS and WebDAV in the default build, and SFTP as an opt-in feature. Deployment options include a one-line install script, Docker and Podman images, Docker Compose files, a Helm chart for Kubernetes, a Nix flake, and an x-cmd entry. Some features are marked as preview, including S3 Tables (Iceberg REST catalog) and MinIO on-disk compatibility.
use_cases: running a private alternative to cloud buckets
data lake and big data object storage
storing backups and media files behind S3 clients
Kubernetes object storage via Helm chart
notable: Written in Rust with a stated focus on memory safety and performance, compared against MinIO in the README
Broad feature set including Object Lock, bitrot protection, pool expansion/decommission, and site replication
Native OpenStack Swift and Keystone authentication support
Apache 2.0 license, contrasted with AGPL in the README
Default web console at port 9001 with a documented default admin login
caveats: Several features are preview or opt-in: S3 Tables, MinIO on-disk compatibility (rio-v2 feature), Swift and SFTP (cargo features)
Objects encrypted by MinIO are not readable by RustFS
Docker bind mounts must be writable by UID/GID 10001:10001 or startup fails; upgrading older root-owned volumes requires manual ownership changes
Single-node single-drive deployments cannot be expanded in place or added as a pool
keywords: store files on my own server
